decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already records the added main-board JST-GH connector, its PWRON source, and the resulting connector count.
The source relies on the existing J_PWR_SIG pin 4 PWRON assignment but does not change the interboard connector pinout or architecture.
Moving the panel-button connector to the main board does not change the board-chain order, power rails, or forwarding behavior.
The panel-button connector and PWRON tap do not affect I2C speed, cabling, pull-ups, or series resistors.
The main-board panel-input inventory necessarily gains a panel-mounted power button connected through a main-board connector.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The power board is no problem, so could you instead add a 2-pin JST-GH connector to the main board for a panel-mounted power button? PWRON already arrives through J\_PWR\_SIG pin 4; the new connector only needs to tap that line so a button can be wired from the enclosure panel.

decisions.reason: The source changes only the panel power-button connector location and does not alter the battery-charge status circuit or indicator.
The source does not answer or change the DCDC1 voltage requirement; the separate voltage question remains unaffected.
Tapping the existing PWRON signal for a panel button does not change the main-board power-source OR-ing method or source selection.
The panel power-button connector does not change standalone USB activation, LDO selection, capacity, or powered scope.
The source does not change the battery connector, its placement, pinout, or NTC connection.
The new connector taps the existing PWRON interboard signal and does not assign or change an ESP32 GPIO.
The panel-button connection does not change the monitored rails, monitor IC, measurement position, or current coverage.
